title: Nafisa Ali Shares Health Update as She Begins Targeted Therapy
excerpt: The veteran actress told followers on Instagram that a PET/CT scan showed new deposits on her liver, and that her medical team has moved her onto targeted therapy.
body:
• Nafisa Ali shared on Instagram on September 13 that a PET/CT scan showed her ovarian/peritoneal cancer has progressed, with new deposits on the surface of her liver.
  • Her medical team has moved her onto targeted therapy, a change in treatment protocol she disclosed publicly from the hospital.
  • The 69-year-old actress was first diagnosed with stage 3 peritoneal and ovarian cancer in November 2018, was declared cancer-free in 2019, and has been documenting a stage 4 recurrence since last year.
  • She has continued working through her treatment, appearing in the 2022 film Uunchai and more recently in Max, Min & Meowzaki.

A candid update from the hospital

Veteran actress Nafisa Ali has shared a candid update on her ongoing cancer treatment, telling her Instagram followers on Sunday, September 13, that her disease has progressed and her medical team has changed her treatment protocol.

https://x.com/ZoomTV/status/2099775055047860233

Posting a photograph of herself from the hospital, Ali wrote: "My treatment protocol has changed and now I have been put on Targeted Therapy... fighting the good fight. Thank you for always keeping my support energy strong." Explaining the change in plain terms, she added: "In very simple terms The PET/CT suggests that the ovarian/peritoneal cancer has progressed, with new deposits on the surface of the liver."

The news, reported by IANS and carried by outlets including Zoom TV, drew a wave of messages from fans wishing her a speedy recovery. Ali has been battling stage 4 peritoneal and ovarian cancer, a diagnosis she has documented with unusual openness for years.

"My treatment protocol has changed and now I have been put on Targeted Therapy... fighting the good fight. Thank you for always keeping my support energy strong."

— Nafisa Ali, in an Instagram post on September 13

Context & background

Ali first went public with her diagnosis of stage 3 peritoneal and ovarian cancer in November 2018. After intensive treatment including surgery and chemotherapy, she was declared cancer-free in 2019. The disease recurred as stage 4 peritoneal cancer last year, and she underwent surgery in April before resuming chemotherapy.

She has shared the journey in strikingly honest terms. In October 2025, she posted pictures of herself bald after chemotherapy, captioning them "Positive Power," and later shared footage of her young granddaughters helping her with her hair loss. In July, she posted that she had completed her 10th chemotherapy session and flown to Goa for a beach walk, writing: "the sea is my healer."

Ali was born on January 18, 1957, in Mumbai. She began her acting career with Shyam Benegal's Junoon in 1979 and has worked in films including Life in a... Metro, Yamla Pagla Deewana, Big B, Bewafa and Major Saab.

Impact & analysis

Ali's public candor about treatment setbacks as well as remissions has made her one of the rare Indian public figures to document a terminal-stage illness in real time. Her posts — from bald selfies to hospital updates — have repeatedly drawn support from colleagues and fans, and her September update continued that pattern of openness rather than retreat.

Even while managing her health, Ali has kept working. In 2022, she appeared in Sooraj Barjatya's Uunchai as the estranged wife of Amitabh Bachchan's character, and she was more recently featured in Max, Min & Meowzaki, according to Zoom TV.

Diaspora angle

For many in the Indian diaspora facing cancer diagnoses in their own families, Ali's public updates have become a touchstone — a well-known face describing scans, protocols and setbacks in language other patients recognize.

What's next

Ali has not disclosed further details about the targeted therapy regimen. Her pattern over the past year suggests she will continue to share updates on her own terms, alongside the work and family moments she has kept part of the story throughout.
